newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stock market tumbles after NAP wins election.
newsitem.headline: Thai stock market tumbles after NAP wins election.

text.p: Thailand's stock market tumbled on Monday on news of the New Aspiration Party's (NAP) election victory and investors waited anxiously for the emergence of the new coalition government's economic team.

The stock market, displaying disapproval of the NAP's win following Sunday's election, lost more than six percent of its value in early morning trade and took the lunch break down 56.83 points, or 5.68 percent, at 943.90.
The fall reversed a two-week rally that had been building in anticipation of a victory for the NAP's archrival, the Democrat Party led by former premier Chuan Leekpai.

The NAP, led by Defence Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, announced on Monday it was forming a coalition with five other parties which mostly belonged to the troubled departing administration of premier Banharn Silpa-archa. Banharn's Chart Thai Party was not included.
Chavalit is expected to be the next premier.
"We have the same old faces, the same team with a new head. It lacks quality," said Preecha Chaijuree of First Asia Securities Plc.
Thai business would have preferred the Democrats because they have a strong economic team of professionals and technocrats, analysts said.
"It's a big let-down for many people. We don't know why we went to the poll to see the same old people return," a radio commentator said.
Some market analysts, however, held out hopes that Chavalit would keep a campaign promise to pick a professional economic team to lift confidence in the government.
Chavalit has said he would name an economic team led by outgoing deputy premier and former banker Amnuay Viravan.

He said the team would have five to six non-elected economists including Narongchai Akrasanee, chairman of General Finance and Securities Plc, and Viroj Putrakul, former chief executive of Lever Brothers in Thailand.
The NAP narrowly beat the Democrats, winning 125 of 393 seats in the lower House of Representatives against 123 collected by the Democrats.
The Democrats proved their popularity among businessmen and urban voters, winning 29 of 37 seats at stake in Bangkok against only one seat picked by NAP.
"It's a shock, a big disappointment but something we have to accept," said Chatchawan Jumruswittayawong, currency dealer at Bank of Ayudhya Plc, reflecting general market feeling.
Brokers and bankers said Chavalit's coalition did not help sentiment as it was mostly the same as the one led by Banharn, who they had blamed for mismanaging the economy in the past 15 months.
The Thai economy is projected to expand about 7.0 percent in 1996, its slowest pace in 10 years. Exports rose 2.4 percent in the first eight months of 1996 against 25 percent a year ago.
Banharn's Chart Thai Party, rocked by mass defections of its members to the NAP after he called snap election in September, regained only 39 of the 92 seats it held.
Banharn showed up at a gathering of NAP's allies on Sunday in a show of support for Chavalit and it was not clear why his party was dropped from Chavalit's alliance.
